title: Progressive traffic dampening and KV reconciliation for intermittent region heartbeat flapping
creator: Ivy Chen
description: Summary: Several customers experienced request failures and elevated latency during intermittent region heartbeat flapping observed on 2026-03-01 (INC-2026-03-01). The root pattern: short-lived control-plane/healthcheck jitter caused downstream dataplane routing to perform aggressive tenant rehomes, which in turn produced KV cache divergence and a spike of 5xxs for heavy-tenant workloads on both Hosted and Dedicated deployments. Goal: implement a safe, observable mitigation (progressive traffic dampening) in the routing layer, add an automated KV reconciliation runner, and update runbooks so SRE/SEs can contain and recover tenants with minimal manual intervention and predictable customer communication.
acceptance_criteria: Routing layer can apply progressive dampening per region with configurable thresholds (RTT, heartbeat misses) and observable state
Automated KV reconciliation job can detect staleness and rehydrate per-tenant caches without full tenant rehome
Runbook updated with step-by-step containment + rollback instructions and an owner for Hosted and Dedicated workflows
Canary rollout shows no >2% increase in 95th percentile latency and reduces 5xx rate caused by rehomes by >= 60% in simulated flapping tests
Customer-facing postmortem checklist and communication templates added to the incident playbook
playbook_steps: 1) Detect: dashboards alert on heartbeat-miss-rate and tenant rehome rate (runbook link)
2) Contain: apply progressive dampening policy for affected region (policy: 1s->3s->10s backoff on repeated misses) via control-plane toggle
3) Validate: monitor tenant-specific 95th latency and 5xxs for 10 minutes
4) Reconcile: schedule KV reconciliation job for tenants with cached inconsistency (batch size configurable)
5) Rollback: if latency or error budget exceeds threshold, revert dampening and escalate to cross-region SRE
6) Communicate: notify customer support + Sales with templated status and ETA
implementation_notes: Routing dampening will be implemented as a middleware for the request router so it is independent of backend type (hosted/dedicated). It exposes metrics: dampening_state, dampen_count, last_heartbeat_ts.
KV reconciliation is implemented as a read-validate-rewrite flow to avoid wholesale cache clears; reconciliation must be idempotent and checkpointed.

We will add a circuit flag 'avoid-rehome' that prevents automated tenant rehomes for tenants flagged during a dampening window. This limits customer impact but raises the chance of local hotspots—trade-off: reduce churn versus hotspots.
Feature flags: ship behind runtime-1.24 feature flag. Canary on 5 dedicated pools and 1 hosted region for 48 hours.
Telemetry: add granular tenant-level tracing for rehome events; retain 7 days of high-res metrics for 48-hour canary windows.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Aggressive dampening reduces churn (fewer rehomes) but can prolong local overloads on degraded nodes—mitigation: use tenant priority and dynamic throttles.
KV reconciliation increases background IO; must be throttled to avoid exacerbating region disks under pressure. Use rate limits and backoff.
Longer dampening windows can hide issues from operators; require an escalation timer to force manual intervention after configurable time.
Customer perception: delaying rehomes may delay error surface reduction for end-users; include customer-facing communication covenant and optional tenant opt-out.
